structured.answer: I'd open an account at Psagot (פסגות) and buy "ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)", because the page puts it first and marks it "הזול". With its numbers (10,000 ₪ now, 500 ₪ a month, 10 years) I'd end up with about 86,492 ₪ in today's money after fees and tax. I didn't change the 10,000 to my own 30,000, so for me the number would be different.

stuck.why: It starts with a big 86,492 and a cut-off number on the right (70,000-something). I wasn't sure which one is 'mine' until I read 'נשאר לכם בעוד 10 שנים'.
The bar is all pink, 5,703, and I had to guess from the legend that pink is מס. So most of the 6,876 'cost' is tax, not fees?
Way too many funds that look alike, plus numbers with minus signs (-43 ₪, -1,268 ₪). I couldn't tell if minus means losing money, so I just took the one the page put on top.
It says 'סכום היום 10,000', but I have 30,000. I left it as it was.

not_found: A clear 'first step: do this' button for opening the account
A place to put my own 30,000 that I'd actually trust myself to use
A plain explanation of what the minus numbers in the fund list mean

findings.what: The fund list has dozens of near-identical rows with lots of coloured tags. Too many options; without the 'הזול' star I'd have done nothing
The minus shekel numbers beside each fund look like losses, and nothing next to them says what they're compared to
The top of the results is cut off/crowded: a big 70,000-something on the right and two 86,4xx numbers next to each other were confusing
The cost bar is mostly tax, but the colour is only explained in a small legend underneath
findings.where: Screen 2, 'כמה זה עולה לכם ב־10 שנים'

findings.what: Jargon in the fund cards (נאמן, משתנים, קבועים, 4D)
The default amount is 10,000, so the big number isn't about my money
Long grey paragraphs I didn't read
Dollar-hedging section is long and full of percentages; that's where I'd close the page
